title: RAW UNREVIEWED: the Kyklaminos jaundice dose is an induced-sweat protocol with an observable output
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. The whole retained critical-text entry II.164 §2 first says jaundice is restored by taking three drachmas with sweet wine or watery hydromel; it then directs that the drinker lie in a warm room and be wrapped in more clothes so that they sweat, and reports the expelled sweat as bile-colored. C0 source-model: dose+vehicle+condition → same drinker placed/wrapped → intended sweating → observed bodily sign. This is an ordered care protocol, not a free “heat” gloss. The remainder of §2 has separate nasal, wool/finger, abdominal, ocular, and rectal uses and is kept separate. Section 2 is present in the critical edition only; the retained Morgan M.652 f72v witness is incomplete and f73r was not acquired, so no complete dated-manuscript attestation is claimed. No Voynich target/group was accessed or bound.

design.mechanism: One explicit patient role (“the drinker”) persists from oral administration through warm-room placement and wrapping to an intended sweat response; the described bile-colored sweat is an observable output. Preserve vehicle alternatives inside the dosing step and keep following application routes distinct.
design.unit: The whole Section 2 block of the complete critical-text II.164 entry in H_COMPLETE_ENTRIES.md. It includes the jaundice dose and sweating protocol, followed in the same source block by several different uses of the juice. The proposed subchain is bounded to the dose-through-sweat clauses; all later nasal, wool/finger, abdomen, eye, and rectal groups stay accounted for as distinct but unresolved branches. Source layer: Wellmann 1907–1914 critical-edition XML cache, not a fresh Latin collation or complete medieval witness transcription. H_SOURCE_METADATA states M.652 f72v is incomplete and f73r was not acquired.
design.contrast: A single scoped intervention trajectory with named drinker and observed output versus an unordered list of remedy ingredients, a heat adjective detached from the patient, or a claim that all subsequent application actions belong to the same recipient/event.
design.prediction: A future authorized whole-unit candidate must bind (a) jaundice as the reason/condition, (b) the root dose and one of two drinks, (c) the same drinker as patient in a warm room with extra wraps, (d) the intended sweat, and (e) the color observation to the produced sweat. No order or value may be borrowed from another route. If the observation is treated as a second medicine or if the patient changes without a written trigger, the candidate fails.
design.scope: Raw C0 source-model only. Paid values: condition=JAUNDICE; amount=3 drachmas; vehicle=one of sweet wine / watery honey-wine; participant=the drinker; care steps=lie in warm room + extra wrapping; intended result=sweating; observed sweat=yellow/bile-colored. Unknown: target identity and any Voynich whole-form family capable of expressing these roles; whether the hue is diagnostic, causal, or a reported confirmation; exact referent of following verbs; how the rest of §2 divides into events. No target data was accessed, so this is not a Voynich reading.
design.predecessors_and_counterexamples: IDEA344 already proposes generic conjunctive condition guards over baths/water/recipient/effect and is a close conceptual predecessor, with missing complete target contract; this card is narrower and anchored to one verbatim dose-care-observation sequence but is not claimed novel from the screen. GDT568 supplies extant owner/action frames but no semantic proof. GDT608 favors whole-form identity over component export, and GDT326 warns against unseen combinations. The nearby root-crossing card AP3_01 has a different operation and opposite conditional outcomes; it does not support this dosing chain. W89 explicitly blocks promoting generic “mix” into a recipe kernel.
